findings.claim: The implemented after-battle morale rule raises campaign morale through combat, against DR29 ('Morale decreases when troops participate in combat'). This happens even when the battle starts at the army's own campaign morale. SupportWorld.OnBattle (SupportWorld.cs:285-289) sets the army's campaign morale to (TacticalResolver end morale + medical restore) × 1,000,000 ÷ MoraleMax, whatever it was before. The TacticalResolver's land morale RECOVERS during battle: +HoldRecovery 20 (Rally 60) per casualty-free pulse, capped at MoraleMax rather than at the start morale (TacticalBattle.cs:1001-1004). So a formation that holds and fights without losses ends above its start, and the campaign inherits the gain. Three of the lane's statements are therefore wrong or misleading. (1) READING M (a) says 'a formation that fights without loss loses none' (support proposal §3.3); it can gain. (2) The D-R1-16 note and limitation 11 attribute morale rises only to the unchecked START half and name M7.15's start-half enforcement as the remedy. Enforcing the start half would not prevent this rise. (3) The 'after-battle half' the lane calls implemented is itself the source.

findings.claim: The support refusal codes do not behave as the proposal's §2.3 table states. Code 4 NegativeTarget can never be produced. OnAllocate decodes kind = B / 2^32 and target = B % 2^32. A negative target only ever arrives with kind 0, which is refused as UnknownKind before the negative check. Worse, any raw order whose decoded kind lies outside 0..255 crashes the support world with an OverflowException instead of being recorded as UnknownKind. An order log is replayed input, so a malformed order makes the world non-runnable instead of refusing and logging it. Codes 5 and 6 are untested (see D-R2-02).
